haiku-low.q1: It creates a login_challenges row and challenge cookie, then redirects to /login/second-factor. No session is created.
haiku-low.q2: Only after a valid code for the pending secret confirms setup or replacement. During replacement, the old secret applies until then.
haiku-low.q3: The recovery code is marked used, the challenge is deleted, and a session starts. An email with the remaining count is queued after commit, and sign-in does not wait for it.
haiku-low.q4: A fifth wrong entry, expiry after 5 minutes, a missing or tampered cookie, or 2FA turned off. The user goes to /login to start again.
haiku-low.q5: Setup confirm deletes all their other sessions. Only the current session stays signed in.
haiku-low.q6: No. A code is accepted only if its step is greater than last_step. Codes for the previous, current, or next 30-second step are accepted.
haiku-low.q7: In one transaction: pending secret becomes active, last_step is set, 10 new hashed recovery codes replace the old ones, and other sessions are deleted. If the update changes zero rows, everything rolls back and the secret stays pending.
haiku-low.q8: A login_challenges row (sha256 of token) plus a sealed, httponly challenge cookie holding the raw token. Removed on success, fifth wrong entry, expiry, missing cookie, or 2FA turned off.
haiku-low.q9: Active secret in totp_factors.secret_sealed, pending secret in pending_secret_sealed, last_step in totp_factors, and recovery codes as hashes in recovery_codes. 2FA is on when secret_sealed is not NULL.
haiku-low.q10: The old secret in secret_sealed still protects sign-in during replacement. Cancel deletes the pending secret, and the old secret and codes stay unchanged.
haiku-low.q11: Exactly one field must be filled: totp_code or recovery_code. Both or neither is a wrong entry. Wrong recovery codes count toward the 5-entry limit.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The user enters the Stuck state, which has no way out in this plan. Support reset and identity checks are undecided.

sonnet.q1: A short-lived challenge (a login_challenges row plus a sealed cookie holding its token), not a session. It grants no access to /home; the user is redirected to /login/second-factor.
sonnet.q2: Once a confirm succeeds with a valid code for the pending secret. The confirm copies the pending secret into secret_sealed (the active secret that sign-in uses). Before that, sign-in ignores the pending secret.
sonnet.q3: The recovery code is marked used, the challenge is deleted in the same transaction, the challenge cookie is cleared and start_session() redirects to /home. After commit, enqueue_email(user_id, "recovery_code_used", {remaining}) is queued with the count of remaining unused codes. Sign-in does not depend on the email: it is not awaited, a failed send is retried in the background, and sign-in is not affected. No remaining count is shown on screen.
sonnet.q4: A 5th wrong entry, expiry (5 minutes), a missing or tampered cookie, or 2FA being turned off. In each case the challenge row (and cookie) is deleted, and the user goes to /login with a message to start again. They re-enter email and password. A cookie that points to no row counts nothing. Stuck (no device and no unused recovery code) has no defined exit.
sonnet.q5: All other sessions of the user are signed out when setup is confirmed (DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ... AND token_hash <> sha256(current cookie)). The current session stays.
sonnet.q6: No. A code is accepted only if its step is greater than last_step, enforced by a conditional UPDATE, so the same code or step cannot pass twice, even for concurrent requests. Drift tolerance is one 30-second step before and one after the current step (three valid steps).
sonnet.q7: In one transaction: (1) a conditional UPDATE copies pending_secret_sealed into secret_sealed, clears the pending secret and sets last_step to the matched step; (2) the user's recovery_codes rows are deleted and 10 new hashed ones inserted, so old codes stop working; (3) all the user's other sessions are deleted. If the conditional UPDATE changes zero rows, the whole transaction rolls back, the secret stays pending, and the form is shown again with "That code did not work. Try again." NOT STATED for any other mid-transaction failure beyond that rollback rule.
sonnet.q8: It is stored as a row in login_challenges (challenge_hash = sha256 of a random token, user_id, expires_at = now plus 5 minutes, failed_attempts). The browser holds the raw token in a sealed, httponly, secure, samesite=Lax challenge cookie with a 5-minute max-age. It is removed by successful sign-in (row deleted in the same transaction, cookie cleared), the 5th wrong entry, expiry found on the next request, 2FA turned off, or a tampered or missing cookie case. Expired rows are not otherwise deleted until the cookie is presented again.
sonnet.q9: All in the totp_factors table, one row per user: secret_sealed (active secret, sealed), pending_secret_sealed (unconfirmed secret, sealed) and last_step (replay protection, per user). Recovery codes are in recovery_codes as sha256 hashes with used_at, never stored raw. 2FA is on when totp_factors.secret_sealed is not NULL.
sonnet.q10: The old secret (secret_sealed) keeps enforcing sign-in, and sign-in ignores the pending secret, until a confirm succeeds. If the user abandons it by cancelling, the pending secret is deleted and the old secret and recovery codes are unchanged. NOT STATED whether an abandoned, un-cancelled pending secret expires; starting again overwrites it.
sonnet.q11: By which form field is filled: totp_code or recovery_code. Exactly one must be filled, and both or neither counts as a wrong entry. Yes, an unknown or already used recovery code is a wrong entry and increments failed_attempts. A correct code is never counted.
sonnet.q12: None is defined. This is the open Stuck state: the user has no way out in this plan. They cannot disable 2FA because disabling needs a code. Whether support may reset 2FA, how identity would be checked and how the user reports the state are not designed.
